# Threads {#sec-threads}

biyos keeps no global state. Everything a call reads or changes belongs to an environment or to a model made on it, so environments are independent of each other and separate threads may use separate environments at the same time. Threads may also share one environment:

- Calls on different models of the environment may run at the same time, from any threads, and so may calls that only read the same model.
- A call that changes a model runs alone on it. Started while another thread is in a call on that model, it fails with `BIYOS_ERR_BUSY` and the message `busy: model: is in a call on another thread`. While it runs, a call on that model from another thread, a read included, fails with `busy: model: is being changed on another thread`. Reading a derivative pattern ([Evaluation](#sec-capi-evaluation)) changes no data of the model but runs alone on it in the same way.
- A call that changes the environment itself, setting one of its options or adding or removing a hook, runs alone on the environment and its models. Started while another thread is in a call on either, it fails with `busy: environment: is in a call on another thread`. While it runs, a call on the environment or on one of its models from another thread fails with `busy: environment: is being changed on another thread`. Creating or copying a model onto the environment is not such a change.
- Freeing a model or the environment is refused in the same way while another thread is in a call on it. Nothing can refuse a call that starts while the free runs or after it returns, since that call would read freed memory, so a program frees an environment or a model only once no other thread is in a call on it or will make one.
- `BIYOS_interrupt` ([Interrupting a call](#sec-threads-interrupt)) and `BIYOS_lasterror` are never refused.

A refused call fails like any other: it changes no model and no option and keeps its error, so the thread that made it may try again once the other call has returned. Under a steady stream of calls from other threads a change may be refused every time, so a program that changes a shared environment or model orders those changes with its other threads itself. A call is refused rather than made to wait, and two calls that would overlap and start at the same moment may both be refused.

A program that wants to change one model from several threads gives each thread a copy ([Copying models](#sec-copy)), on the same environment or on another. `BIYOS_copymdl` only reads the source, so other threads may read it meanwhile. Afterwards the two are apart.

An environment keeps a last error per thread ([The last error](#sec-errors-message)), so a thread reads the failure of its own last failed call, never one another thread left, together with the model that call was on.

biyos starts no thread of its own yet. `BIYOS_version` reads no state and may be called from any thread. A hook runs on the thread whose call sent the event, so the calls that read or format an event run there too. The hooks of an environment run one at a time: an event sent from one thread waits while a hook runs for another, so a hook needs no lock of its own, and `BIYOS_getevtmdl` tells which model each event came from. The hooks of a model run one at a time in the same way, but beside the hooks of other models and of the environment, so data they share with those hooks needs a lock. An event of a call on a model waits for the hooks of the model and then for those of the environment, never for both at once. A hook must not wait for a call on another thread that sends an event it receives, since that call waits for the hook. A call a hook makes on another environment may wait for that environment's hooks, so hooks of two environments must not call into each other from two threads.

## Interrupting a call {#sec-threads-interrupt}

`BIYOS_interrupt` asks the call running on an environment to stop. Any thread may call it while another thread is inside a call on that environment or on one of its models, and so may a signal handler, since it only sets a flag and returns. A long call reads the flag where it checks its time limits and stops with the termination `BIYOS_TRM_STOP`, an outcome rather than an error code. The flag clears when the next call on the environment or on one of its models starts, a refused one included, so a request that arrives after a call has returned does not stop the one that follows. A call made by a hook leaves it set, so a hook may stop the call that sent its event. No call is long enough to read the flag yet.

## In Python {#sec-threads-python}

The package calls the library through `ctypes`, which releases the global interpreter lock for the length of each C call, so threads that work on separate environments run their C code side by side. In Python, one environment and its models are used by one thread at a time.

```{.python file="interfaces/python/examples/threads.py"}
```

Each thread builds its own model on its own environment, and the results come back in the order the work was given, whatever order the threads finished in. A hook written in Python takes the interpreter lock while it runs.

`Env.interrupt` makes the request that [Interrupting a call](#sec-threads-interrupt) describes, and another thread may call it while a call runs. A `KeyboardInterrupt` raised in a hook makes it too, and is raised once the call returns.
